zones.name: Columbia Zone
zones.html:
Columbia River

Salmon and steelhead

Fall Season (August 1 – December 31)

For all mainstem fall-season salmon/steelhead fisheries between Buoy 10 and the Highway 395 Bridge (Pasco, WA), each legal angler aboard a vessel may continue to use angling gear until the daily adult salmon/steelhead bag limit for all legal anglers aboard has been achieved. However, no individual angler may exceed any personal daily bag limit. Anglers are reminded that it is unlawful to fish in an area while in possession of fish that are not legal for that area.

Buoy 10 upstream to west Puget Island

Area definition: From the Buoy 10 line upstream to a line at the west end of Puget Island extending from green navigation marker #39 on the Washington shore to green navigation marker #41, then to red navigation marker #42, and terminating at red navigation marker #44A on the Oregon shore.

General regulations during fall season:

  • The Tongue Point/Rocky Point line is defined as: a line projected from Rocky Point on the Washington shore through red navigation buoy #44 to the navigation marker at Tongue Point on the Oregon shore.
  • Between Buoy 10 and the Tongue Point/Rocky Point line, from August 1 – September 30, the adult coho minimum size is 16-inches.
  • Between Buoy 10 and the Tongue Point/Rocky Point line, retention of jack salmon is prohibited through September 30. Permanent regulations regarding adult and jack length definitions are in effect, with the exception of the adult coho minimum size as referenced above for this section of the Buoy 10 fishing area.
  • Wild coho must be released.
  • All steelhead must be released August 1 – October 31.

Additional regulations by date period:

  • August 1–9: Retention of Chinook and hatchery coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • August 10 – September 2: Retention of hatchery Chinook and hatchery coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery salmon (Chinook or coho), but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 3–11: Retention of hatchery coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery coho.
  • September 12 – October 31: Retention of hatchery coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is three hatchery coho.
  • November 1 – December 31: Retention of hatchery coho and hatchery steelhead allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery salmon/steelhead (coho and steelhead only).
Boundary line at west Puget Island

West Puget Island upstream to Warrior Rock/Bachelor Island

Area definition: From a line at the west end of Puget Island extending from green navigation marker #39 on the Washington shore to green navigation marker #41, then to red navigation marker #42, and terminating at red navigation marker #44A on the Oregon shore upstream to a line projected from the Warrior Rock lighthouse on the Oregon shore to the marker atop the piling dolphin located at the downstream end of Bachelor Island on the Washington shore. Note: the definition of the Warrior Rock/Bachelor Island line changed beginning in 2025.

General regulations during fall season:

  • All steelhead must be released August 1 – October 31.

Additional regulations by date period:

  • August 1 – September 2: Retention of Chinook and hatchery coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 3–30: Salmon/steelhead angling prohibited.
  • October 1–15: Retention of coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two coho.
  • October 16–31: Retention of hatchery coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery coho.
  • November 1 – December 31: Retention of hatchery coho and hatchery steelhead allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery salmon/steelhead (coho and steelhead only).
Warrior Rock/Bachelor Island boundary line

Warrior Rock/Bachelor Island upstream to Bonneville Dam

Area definition: From a line projected from the Warrior Rock lighthouse on the Oregon shore to the marker atop the piling dolphin located at the downstream end of Bachelor Island on the Washington shore upstream to Bonneville Dam. Note: the definition of the Warrior Rock/Bachelor Island line changed beginning in 2025.

General regulations during fall season:

  • All steelhead must be released August 1 – October 31.

Additional regulations by date period:

  • August 1 – September 11: Retention of Chinook and hatchery coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 12–15: Retention of Chinook and coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 16–30: Salmon/steelhead angling prohibited.
  • October 1–15: Retention of coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two coho.
  • October 16–31: Retention of hatchery coho allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery coho.
  • November 1 – December 31: Retention of hatchery coho and hatchery steelhead allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two hatchery salmon/steelhead (coho and steelhead only).

Bonneville Dam upstream to The Dalles Dama

General regulations during fall season:

  • All steelhead must be released August 1 – October 31.
  • Wild coho caught downstream of the Hood River Bridge from August 1 – September 11 and October 16 – December 31 must be released.

Additional regulations by date period:

  • August 1 – September 15: Retention of Chinook and coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 16–30: Salmon/steelhead angling prohibited.
  • October 1–31: The retention of coho is allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two coho.
  • November 1 – December 31: Retention of coho and hatchery steelhead allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon/steelhead (coho and steelhead only).

The Dalles Dam upstream to the Oregon/Washington border (upstream of McNary Dam)a

General regulations during fall season:

  • All steelhead must be released September 1 – December 31.

Additional regulations by date period:

  • August 1–31: Retention of Chinook, coho, and hatchery steelhead allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon/steelhead, but only one may be a Chinook and only one may be a hatchery steelhead.
  • September 1–15: Retention of Chinook and coho allowed. The daily adult bag limit is two salmon, but only one may be a Chinook.
  • September 16–30: Salmon/steelhead angling prohibited.
  • October 1 – December 31: The retention of coho is allowed; all Chinook must be released. The daily adult bag limit is two coho.

a Temporary rules for Thermal Angling Sanctuaries associated with Eagle Creek, Herman Creek, and the Deschutes River are described below.

  • July 15 – September 15: Closed to angling.
  • September 16 – December 31: See rules for Columbia River mainstem: The Dalles Dam upstream to the Oregon/Washington border (upstream of McNary Dam).
